fcev_battery_policy.source: Toyota second-generation Mirai, manufacturer announcement of 30 November 2020: 310.8 V, 4 Ah (1.2432 kWh), complete pack 44.6 kg, 31.5 kW discharge for 10 seconds. https://newsroom.toyota.eu/introducing-the-all-new-toyota-mirai/
fcev_battery_policy.sizing: Nominal energy and complete pack mass scale together with the required DC buffer power divided by 31.5 kW, inside native mass/power sizing.
fcev_battery_policy.power_boundary: Manufacturer discharge rating is for 10 seconds; no continuous discharge or charging limit is inferred.
fcev_battery_policy.mass_boundary: Complete pack 44.6 kg per 1.2432 kWh; the existing cell fraction and NMC-622 manufacture are retained allocation proxies, not measured Mirai cell specifications.
fcev_battery_policy.limits: Regenerative charging remains unconstrained by a battery-specific rating. SOC, fuel-cell ramp response, thermal limits and battery ageing are not certified by this calibration.
fcev_battery_policy.lca_proxy: Approved MIX capacity market uses nominal kWh, including replacements and end of life, with a documented physical mass mismatch: a smaller kWh purchase does not establish less material in the heavier high-power pack.
fcev_battery_policy.future_hardware: Premise retains complete 2020 FCEV hardware in future scenarios; fuel demand follows the scenario efficiency trend.

phev_battery_replacement_policy.distance_basis: total vehicle distance, not electric-mode distance
phev_battery_replacement_policy.formula: max(0, lifetime km / battery lifetime km - 1, lifetime km / annual km / 18 - 1)
